report:
PASS applies to the restricted A–G comparison and the mathematical claims of the entire author manuscript. Every restricted essential inference and support edge is established. The original P13 completion criterion remains INCONCLUSIVE: no general coexistence theorem, closed positive construction from arbitrary coexistence, or flow existence/convergence theorem is proved. The supplied candidate=false and historical first original review INCONCLUSIVE remain unchanged. Literature priority is not certified.

I checked the supplied proofs independently and opened [Bedford–Taylor, §2](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf) and [Tosatti–Weinkove, Corollary 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390v2). Their operator conversions are respectively D=4πdd^c and v=2πφ. Protected artifacts were not inspected. Execution receipts, hashes and computations are not correctness premises.

A: Positivity yields measure coefficients and a positive Hermitian density Q against a common coefficient-dominating measure ν. With the manuscript's conventions, direct substitution gives Γ₀(T)=n(n!)^(−1/n)(v det Q)^(1/n)ν, where dV=vλ. The auxiliary metric cancels completely. For the untransposed coefficient convention and coframe change θ′=Lθ, Q′=bar(L)QLᵗ and v′=v/|det L|²; hence v′det Q′=v det Q. The independent note's transposed convention instead gives LQL*, with the same determinant cancellation. Changing domination to a common measure rescales Q by its Radon–Nikodym factor t, and det(tQ)^(1/n)=t det(Q)^(1/n), including t=0. This handles extraneous dominating mass, mutually singular coefficients and rank deficiency. AM–GM bounds Γ₀ by a smooth bounded multiple of a reference trace measure, proving compact Radon finiteness without closedness. Cofactor algebra also verifies the smooth-root formula and every ordinary-wedge factorial.

B: A sufficiently large local smooth psh correction q makes w+q genuinely bounded psh; it does not make β a local curvature form. Set S=dd^c(w+q), R=dd^c q and define E^b by the signed bounded-product expansion of (S−R)^b. For each closed mixed factor U, the bounded recursion gives dd^c[(w+q)U]=S∧U, while smooth differentiation gives dd^c(qU)=R∧U. Subtraction proves E^b=dd^c[wE^(b−1)]. Induction in this recursion proves correction and overlap independence because the canonical multiplier w and the preceding order-zero current agree on overlaps.

The actual Hermitian product is the resulting binomial expansion with smooth β factors. Its positivity can be checked using decreasing local psh mollifications: β+dd^c w_j≥−δ_j e with δ_j→0. Corrected positive smooth powers converge to that expansion by bounded-product continuity and local mass bounds. Thus the argument concerns actual bounded products, rather than formal wedges. For a+b=n and b≥1, distributional pairing gives ∫β^a∧E^b=⟨wE^(b−1),dd^c(β^a)⟩=0. Closed E factors remove mixed derivatives; a=0 uses dd^c1=0. Exactly the stated all-lower-power hypotheses therefore give mass V for every bounded canonical potential and both extrema V. Smooth expansion gives all required dd^c(A^j)=0 identities and ∫β∧A^(n−1)=V. No dβ=0 assumption enters.

C: Integration by parts against every dd^c-closed current proves equality of the actual normalized sets under h=β+dd^c u; A then gives equality of their entire intrinsic measure families. For smooth r>0, the stated F is smooth and the Hermitian existence theorem applies. With v=2πφ, the independently proved mass identity forces e^bV=V for the manuscript's normalized F, hence b=0. The independent reconstruction's alternative F differs by the constant log(V/M) and yields the identical equation A^n=Vr^n dV/M.

For every admissible current, including singular coefficient parts, AM–GM gives rΓ₀(T)≤(M/V)^(1/n)A∧T. Its right-hand trace has integral one. Smooth-test approximation and L^n duality consequently identify Γ₀(T)=k_T dV and prove the claimed critical norm bound; absolute continuity is derived, not assumed. B makes T_r=A^(n−1)/V genuinely dd^c-closed and normalized. Its density is exactly V^(−1/n)r^(n−1)/‖r‖_n^(n−1), attaining the smooth endpoint. Positive smooth approximation with the common dual bound proves the supremum for every real or complex L^n root, including the trivial zero case. Arbitrary positive smooth probability dV and all currents are retained.

D: The operator gives dd^c u(x₁)=u″β₁/(4π), verifying the displayed cosine perturbation. Periodicity, closedness, ε≤a_ε≤2−ε, global minimum eigenvalue ε, the upper bound 2β and every fixed-order coefficient/potential bound follow directly. The smooth limit loses rank at x₁=0,1/2. Ordinary wedges give V=n!, and B–C give both bounded mass extrema and identical full current/determinant data. The global dz_j frame proves triviality of the canonical bundle and real c₁=0. Every positive member is already Kähler, balanced and pluriclosed.

E: The real expression for ξ and the sign of dh_τ are correct. Write Ω_ε=q+η, where q occupies the first complex surface and η is the remaining closed flat form. Explicitly, ξ²=−2β₁β₂, q²=2(a_ε−τ²s²)β₁β₂ and q³=0. Thus Ω_ε^j=η^j+jqη^(j−1)+binom(j,2)q²η^(j−2), omitting unavailable terms. Both dd^c q and dd^c q² vanish, so every required power identity holds in every dimension, including n=2; a=1 gives the corresponding h_τ calculation.

The block of Ω_ε−εβ has nonnegative diagonals and determinant [2(1−ε)²−τ²]s²≥0 in the exact parameter ranges. Equality of the minimum eigenvalue with ε occurs at s=0, and the block trace gives Ω_ε≤3β. Integration yields V_τ=n!(1−τ²/2) and balanced trace n!. The fixed nonzero exterior derivative, uniform fixed-order smooth bounds and rank-deficient smooth limit are verified. These directly checked hypotheses justify every B–C application, including both masses and the full endpoint for arbitrary fixed smooth probability dV. The separate balanced metric is the flat β on the already-Kähler torus.

F: The Fourier series gives w_ε″=4π(f_ε−1), positivity and mean f_ε=1. Hence k_Tε=V^(−1/n)f_ε^((n−1)/n), its critical-power integral is V^(−1/(n−1)), and the varying root p_ε=f_ε^(1/n) has unit L^n norm and attains the all-current endpoint. Absolute summability proves |w_ε|≤π/3 and uniform convergence. The limit equals the continuous periodic quadratic −2π(x²−x+1/6), whose second derivative is 4πδ₀−4π. Thus its first-coordinate curvature is S₀=δ_{x₁=0}dx₁∧dy₁, with a genuine bounded local subharmonic potential.

One-coordinate decreasing regularization proves S₀²=0 in the actual bounded-product sense. Consequently A₀^k=η^k+kS₀η^(k−1), proving the claimed product-current limit, normalization and genuine top-degree mass V. Against common domination by Lebesgue and hypersurface measures, T₀'s two coefficient matrices have ranks one and n−1; both determinants vanish. Thus Γ₀(T₀)=0 in every n≥2.

Let ν be the hypersurface probability measure. The three measures have distinct limits: A_ε^n=Vf_εdV converges weakly to Vν=A₀^n; k_Tε^(n/(n−1))dV converges weakly to V^(−1/(n−1))ν although the limit current's power density is zero; Γ₀(T_ε) tends to zero in total mass. The last assertion follows by splitting off a small neighborhood E and using ∫_E f_ε^((n−1)/n)dV≤dV(E)^(1/n). Almost-everywhere convergence of f_ε to zero with fixed integral proves failure of uniform integrability of the critical powers. The note's trace formula [1+(n−1)f_ε]dV/n is also correct. The supplementary quadrature values agree with independent numerical evaluation but are unnecessary for these proofs.

G: D and E provide actual families with identical complete determinant data, constant positive bounded mass extrema, real c₁=0 and uniform fixed-order smooth bounds, yet global minimum eigenvalue ε→0. E additionally retains a separate balanced metric and fixed nonzero exterior derivative. This establishes the stated uniform-estimate obstruction. A pointwise determinant lower bound δ together with a metric upper bound Λ would give λ_min≥δ/Λ^(n−1); the fixed determinant profile supplies no such δ. Scalar perturbations preserve the exterior derivative. No flow evolution is constructed, and ε is not flow time. Additional density, torsion-norm or initial pointwise flow controls are not excluded.

The actual support lists are n1:[]; n2:[]; n3:[n1]; n4:[n1,n2,n3]; n5:[n3,n4]; n6:[n3,n4,n5]; n7:[n2,n3,n4,n5]; n8:[n1,n4,n5,n6,n7]. All 18 applications were checked: the analytic imports support n3–n4; intrinsic algebra and mass identities supply n4's normalization and endpoint; n5–n6 establish their hypotheses before applying those results; n7 uses the intrinsic formula, actual bounded products, sharp bound and torus normalization; n8 uses the proved examples and elementary eigenvalue algebra. There is no circular, dangling or unresolved mathematical edge.

Harmless wording clarifications: tr(P_h)=n holds σ_h-almost everywhere; the concentration family's smooth potentials are uniformly bounded in C⁰, with no uniform derivative bounds asserted; ‘least eigenvalue ε’ denotes the global minimum; and the concentration maximizers concern the sharp critical norm and varying dual roots, not a single fixed root. Uniform ellipticity means one lower bound for the entire family. These require no substantive repair.

The additional all-lower-power hypothesis of B–C is never established from arbitrary balanced/pluriclosed coexistence. The examples therefore prove the restricted obstruction while leaving the original geometric and flow completion criteria unresolved.

passages.statement: For 1≤k≤n and locally bounded plurisubharmonic v₁,…,v_k on a coordinate ball Ω⊂Cⁿ, with D=2i∂bar∂, the recursively defined products Dv₁∧⋯∧Dv_k=D[v₁ Dv₂∧⋯∧Dv_k] are positive d-closed order-zero currents, symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly under componentwise decreasing sequences with locally bounded psh limits. Bedford–Taylor (1982), equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

For 1≤k≤n and locally bounded plurisubharmonic v₁,…,v_k on a coordinate ball Ω⊂Cⁿ, with D=2i∂bar∂, the recursively defined products Dv₁∧⋯∧Dv_k=D[v₁ Dv₂∧⋯∧Dv_k] are positive d-closed order-zero currents, symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly under componentwise decreasing sequences with locally bounded psh limits. Bedford–Taylor (1982), equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

For 1≤k≤n and locally bounded plurisubharmonic v₁,…,v_k on a coordinate ball Ω⊂Cⁿ, with D=2i∂bar∂, the recursively defined products Dv₁∧⋯∧Dv_k=D[v₁ Dv₂∧⋯∧Dv_k] are positive d-closed order-zero currents, symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly under componentwise decreasing sequences with locally bounded psh limits. Bedford–Taylor (1982), equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

For 1≤k≤n, if v_j^a↓v^a for a=0,…,k on a coordinate ball Ω⊂Cⁿ, with every function locally bounded psh, then v_j^0 Dv_j^1∧⋯∧Dv_j^k converges weakly as order-zero currents to v^0 Dv^1∧⋯∧Dv^k, where D=2i∂bar∂. Bedford–Taylor (1982), Theorem 2.4.

For a Euclidean ball Ω⊂Cⁿ, compact K⊂Ω, 1≤k≤n and bounded psh v₁,…,v_k, there is C=C(K,Ω,n,k) such that ∫_K Dv₁∧⋯∧Dv_k∧e^(n−k)≤C∏ₐ‖vₐ‖∞, with D=2i∂bar∂ and e=(i/2)Σ dz_j∧dbar z_j. Bedford–Taylor (1982), Theorem 2.10.

On a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n≥2 with a smooth positive Hermitian form ω, every smooth real F admits a unique real b and a unique smooth real φ satisfying (ω+i∂bar∂φ)^n=e^(F+b)ω^n, ω+i∂bar∂φ>0 and sup_X φ=0. No d-closedness of ω is required. Tosatti–Weinkove, arXiv:0910.1390v2, Corollary 1.
passages.quote: For every smooth real-valued function F on M there exists a unique real number b and a unique smooth real-valued function ϕ
